capabilities_done: host.rs Pool::exchange: every reply FRAME is compared with the container-declared (width, height) (Call.declared, taken from VideoStreamSpec in open_session via WorkerSession.declared) by within_declared_size BEFORE on_frame hands it to reel's route; a larger picture under the reply cap is Failure::Protocol: protocol_faults +1, worker terminated, Av1Error::Worker(Protocol) with the fault slot filled, no picture delivered. Reel's Forward check stays as defence in depth. Smaller pictures stay legal (AV1-ISOBMFF 2.2.4 / Matroska V_AV1 declare the sequence maximum) and a side declared as 0 is not checked. The OversizeFrame (over the reply cap) path is unchanged and still ends as decoder_output_too_large / killed_oversize. (471b679)

host.rs Pool::exchange: a FRAME reply is taken only for a batch request (arm guard want == Want::BatchEnd); a FRAME answering OPEN falls to the existing catch-all arm: Failure::Protocol, protocol_faults +1, worker terminated, Av1Error::Worker(Protocol) with the fault slot filled (through the Registry route: ReelError::DecoderFault{Protocol}, counted). The open_session closure that used to refuse it (uncounted Av1Error::Reel) stays as a second refusal; module docs gain a protocol bullet citing the tests. (a024461)

test-faults only (V4-04): WorkerTestFault::OversizePicture (every decoded frame answered 2 pixels wider, zeroed planes, 18x16 against the 16x16 fixtures, 483 bytes on the wire against a reply cap of 896), WorkerTestFault::UndersizePicture (2 pixels narrower and lower, 14x14) and WorkerTestFault::FrameOnOpen (OPEN answered with a well-formed 2x2 mono FRAME, wire::encode_tiny_frame behind av1-worker + test-faults); worker.rs Faults::reshape is called from flush_batch through a cfg(feature = test-faults) parameter and Faults::on_open from the OPEN arm, so a product worker has neither hook

route_notes.shared_tree_state: when this lane started the shared edit tree held another builder's uncommitted, non-compiling hsk-studio-reel edits (isobmff.rs missing clean_aperture and field_info), so reel-native could not build there; all runs used the scratch tree above and each commit is a pathspec commit of crates/hsk-studio-reel-native from the shared tree (content compared with the green scratch crate: identical modulo line endings).
route_notes.retry_guard: Expected-failure red runs (R3, R4, R5) were each followed by an identical-command run that the retry guard blocked (same normalized command, same shared-tree HEAD, same gameplan digest): R3 and R4 against the R2 failure, and the a024461 green run against the R5 failure. Route taken every time: no flag or filter change and no gameplan step; the guard key is the shared-tree HEAD (confirm root = wt-studio-assets), so the run was repeated unchanged once another builder's commit moved that HEAD. Not a product failure and not an infrastructure cause, so no gameplan step was added.
